claim: Let \(B=(B_t)_{0\le t\le1}\) be a standard Brownian bridge from \(0\) to \(0\), with local time normalized by the occupation-density formula, and put \(L=L_1^0\), \(I_0=1\), and \(I_q=\int_0^1 B_t^{2q}\,dt\) for integers \(q\ge1\). For every integer \(q\ge0\), \[\operatorname{Cov}(L,I_q)=\sqrt{\pi/2}\,\frac{q!}{2^q(2q+1)}\left(\frac{\binom{2q+2}{q+1}}{2^{2q+1}}-1\right).\] Thus the covariance is zero at \(q=0\) and strictly negative for every \(q\ge1\).

integrity.computational_status: No numerical experiment is used as proof; low-order substitutions are algebraic consistency checks.
integrity.privacy_status: Public content contains mathematical statements and bibliographic references only.
integrity.proof_basis: Analytic Gaussian conditioning and beta-function integration.

scientific_limitations: The theorem concerns a standard unit bridge, occupation-density local time at zero, and integer even powers only.
It gives covariances, not a joint distribution, correlation coefficients, or a general dependence theorem for arbitrary path functionals.
The full text of one closely related conditional-area paper was not available in the inspected sources; indirect coverage remains a literature risk.
title: Exact local-time covariance hierarchy for Brownian-bridge power energies
